transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're recovering?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that. I also wanted to ask when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. It's safe to continue using your eye drops or gel for dry eyes - you can use them again as they were prescribed before your surgery, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That’s good to know, thank you. I'm also experiencing a lot of sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some light sensitivity is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses, and it should improve over time. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. Do you have any redness or pain along with the light sensitivity?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, there's no redness or pain, just the light sensitivity. Thank you for the advice. I do have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common to have blurry vision in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How many days or weeks have you had since your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about a week since the surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's normal then - it's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery. It should improve quickly from here and get clearer over the coming days and weeks.

However, if your vision stays blurry or gets significantly worse, let us know and we can check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that covers everything I was wondering about. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best wishes with your recovery!

verdict.label: pass

Finally, `escalation_criteria` was covered with, "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further." All points were covered.
